rd.text: Research and development costs increased by $6.2 million, or 16%, to $45.8 million during the three months ended June 30, 2025 from $39.5 million during the three months ended June 30, 2024. There was also an increase of $3.5 million in material and supplies costs primarily due to Eclipse program development, and an increase of $1.8 million in depreciation and amortization expenses related to the completion of test stands and manufacturing facilities that were placed in service during the current year period.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net increased by $1.5 million, or 40%, to $5.2 million during the three months ended June 30, 2025 from $3.7 million during the three months ended June 30, 2024. This increase primarily reflects a $2.3 million decrease in non-cash interest expense related to interest capitalized, resulting from decreased construction in progress period over period resulting from the placement into service of several major assets during 2024. In addition, there was a $1.0 million increase in debt issuance cost amortization from the Company’s entrance into the third amendment to the Term Loan Facility in May 2024. These increases were offset by a $1.8 million increase in interest income driven by a more efficient capital structure, including higher yields from money market holdings.

fcf.heading: Free Cash Flow
fcf.text:
Free Cash Flow is a non-GAAP financial measure. We define Free Cash Flow as net cash used in operating activities, less purchases of property and equipment. We believe that Free Cash Flow is a meaningful indicator of liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated from or used in operations that, after purchases of property and equipment, can be used for strategic initiatives, including continuous investment in our business and strengthening our balance sheet.

Free Cash Flow has limitations as a liquidity measure, and you should not consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our cash flows as reported under U.S. GAAP. Free Cash Flow may be affected in the near to medium term by the timing of capital investments, fluctuations in our growth and the effect of such fluctuations on working capital, and changes in our cash conversion cycle.

We expect to continue investing in research and development and, accordingly, expect our research and development expenses to vary as we continue to invest in developing and improving our services, and as our products reach technological feasibility and full-rate production.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased by $2.3 million, or 59%, to $1.6 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $4.0 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. Interest expense during the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily comprised of interest related to the Term Loans.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: Our provision for income taxes consists of an estimate for federal and state income taxes based on enacted rates, as adjusted for allowable credits, deductions, uncertain tax positions, changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities, and changes in the tax law. We maintain a valuation allowance to offset all federal and state net deferred tax assets, as realization of such assets does not meet the more-likely-than-not threshold required under ASC 740, Income Taxes .

ocf.heading: Net Cash Used in Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities increased by $76.1 million, or 55%, to $213.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $137.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net loss, exclusive of non-cash items, increased by $41.1 million in the current period. This was primarily due to increases in labor and contractor costs, purchases of materials used in the manufacturing and development of our products, and general corporate expenses. In addition, net working capital used in operating activities increased by $35.0 million, which was primarily driven by the timing and recognition of prepaid launch services. Depending on the volume of work performed and the various stages of completion of our projects, our working capital balances will fluctuate throughout the year due to the timing of cash payments and cash receipts.

da.text: Research and Development – includes employee and contractor compensation, supplies and materials for new service development, depreciation and amortization, and regulatory compliance costs. Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. We expect to continue investing in research and development and, accordingly, expect our research and development expenses to vary as we continue to invest in developing and improving our services, and as our products reach technological feasibility and full-rate production.

wc.text: Our working capital position was in a surplus as of September 30, 2026, in which our current assets exceeded our current liabilities. We often make advanced payments to suppliers for goods or services that have not yet been received that are recorded as current or non-current assets depending on whether they are expected to be settled within a year. Additionally our current deferred revenue totaled $171.2 million as of September 30, 2026. This is primarily due to the timing and nature of our deferred revenue where advanced payments and billings in excess of revenues recognized are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized into revenue as we satisfy the underlying performance obligation. Due to the nature of our supplier and customer contracts as well as the timing of payments, we expect to continue to fluctuate between a surplus and a deficit of net working capital.

capex.text: During the nine months ended September 30, 2025, net cash used by investing activities consisted of $20.8 million in purchases of property and equipment.

fcf.heading: Free Cash Flow
fcf.text:
Free Cash Flow is a non-GAAP financial measure. We define Free Cash Flow as net cash used in operating activities, less purchases of property and equipment and internal-use software. We believe that Free Cash Flow is a meaningful indicator of liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated from or used in operations, after purchases of property and equipment and internal-use software, that (after any debt service requirements or other non-discretionary expenditures not otherwise deducted from the measure) can be used for strategic initiatives, including continuous investment in our business and strengthening our balance sheet.

Free Cash Flow has limitations as a liquidity measure, and you should not consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our cash flows as reported under U.S. GAAP. Free Cash Flow may be affected in the near to medium term by the timing of capital investments, fluctuations in our growth and the effect of such fluctuations on working capital and changes in our cash conversion cycle.

intro.text: Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company that enables government and commercial customers to launch, land, and operate in space – anywhere, anytime. As the partner of choice for responsive space missions, Firefly is the first commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with approximately 24-hour notice. Firefly is also the only company to achieve a fully successful landing on the Moon. Established in 2017, Firefly’s engineering, manufacturing, and test facilities are co-located in central Texas to enable rapid innovation. The company’s small- to medium-lift launch vehicles, lunar landers, and orbital vehicles are built with common flight-proven technologies to enable speed, reliability, and cost efficiencies for each mission from low Earth orbit to the Moon and beyond. For more information, visit www.fireflyspace.com .

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Major customers are defined as those individually comprising more than 10 % of the Company’s total revenue.
The Company’s customers that accounted for 10 % or more of the total accounts receivable, were as follows:

We may not actually achieve the plans, intentions or expectations disclosed in our forward-looking statements, and you should not rely on our forward-looking statements in making your investment decision.
Critical civil and national security infrastructure on Earth depends on satellite systems in space, and threats from adversaries have been on the rise.
While we often source raw materials and other inputs and services from multiple sources, in some cases we also purchase various inputs and services from a sole or single source.

We rely upon a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, copyrights, confidentiality procedures, contractual commitments, and other legal rights to establish and protect our intellectual property.
• Our operations depend on our manufacturing facilities, which are subject to physical and other risks.
• We are a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq rules and we rely on exemptions from certain corporate governance requirements.
Our own growth relies on our ability to add new launch sites, which could be delayed by business or regulatory challenges.

We obtain certain of our hardware components, various subsystems and systems and other products and services from a limited group of suppliers and vendors, some of which are sole source suppliers and vendors.

Although we hold long-term non-binding contracts with certain key suppliers that establish pricing, minimize lead times and to some degree mitigate risk, we do not have long-term agreements with all suppliers that obligate them to continue to sell components, products required to build our systems, or products to us.
In addition, credit constraints of key suppliers could result in accelerated payment of accounts payable by us, adversely impacting our cash flow.

Furthermore, we believe continued budget pressures could have serious negative consequences for the security of the U.S., the defense industrial base and the customers, employees, suppliers, investors, and communities that rely on companies in the defense industrial base.
